final:
I checked all 7 issues against the code. Two need a change, two are worth considering, and three are wrong. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json` (the JSON is valid). I didn't change any code or post any replies.

| # | Issue | Verdict | Actionable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Frontend device-limit setting has no type annotation | VALID | YES |
| 1 | Race between counting devices and inserting a new one | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 2 | "Zero rows updated" reported as limit reached | INVALID | NO |
| 3 | Duplicate 30-day expiration constant | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 4 | Time skew in the limit check | INVALID | NO |
| 5 | Test doesn't check that existing devices can still update | VALID | YES |
| 6 | Test device has no `CreatedAt` | INVALID | NO |

- **#0:** strict mode is on, so `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97`) gets the type `undefined`. It still compiles against the interface, so the build doesn't break. But code reading the setting gets the wrong type. The one-line fix is `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`.
- **#1:** the count (`database.go:109-118`) and the insert run as separate, unlocked database calls. Two new devices arriving at once, or several Grafana instances, can each see room under the limit and both insert. The limit can be exceeded slightly, but nothing is corrupted.
- **#2:** the update only runs once the limit is already reached. At that point, zero rows updated means a new or expired device is being refused, which is the intended behavior. The MySQL "unchanged row counts as 0" concern doesn't apply: the connection sets `clientFoundRows=true` (`sqlstore.go:287`).
- **#3:** there are actually three copies of the 30-day window: `database.go:16`, `api/api.go:18`, and `thirtyDays` in `impl.go:25`, which the reviewer missed.
- **#4:** the device's timestamp is set a few microseconds before the check runs, and the window has a 1-minute margin, so the gap has no effect.
- **#5:** the new test only covers rejecting a new device. Nothing tests that an already-registered device can still update once the limit is hit. That matters, because when the limit error comes back, anonymous login fails.
- **#6:** the test that already existed also leaves `CreatedAt` unset and passes on every database in CI. The limit logic only looks at `updated_at`.
